proposal.title: Anchor-Stable Mask-Shortcut Suppression for HistGradientBoosting under Missingness Shift (proposed hypothesis)
proposal.hypothesis: When test missingness depends on a feature's own value (MNAR) and is shifted relative to training, HGB trained with native NaN learns mask-to-label shortcuts whose sign can flip at test time. We propose the following narrow assumption: P(y | x_obs) for value-informative structure changes under shift, while P(y | anchors x0, x1) does not. Under that assumption, a predictor that removes the label information carried by the mask beyond what the anchors explain should improve held-out mean AP relative to native-NaN HGB and random-mask augmentation. We do not claim this works for arbitrary MNAR.
proposal.mechanism: Causal edge targeted: M -> Yhat shortcut (atom_42235e794c05a946, atom_a7b4cd2b88c13161). Training mixes two regimes. The first is native NaN on observed MCAR rows. The second is value-preserving remasking, where the mask pattern is resampled independently of y conditional on the anchors. A mask-invariance penalty is approximated by averaging predictions across K resampled masks, which follows the posterior integration idea in atom_3cca467611d75e87. Only observed values and masks are used. No target-batch statistics are used.

proposed_primitives.definition: For each training row, resample the additional mask M' using a rate drawn from rate ~ g(anchor bin) estimated on training data. M' is independent of y given the anchors. The final mask is M_total = M_obs OR M'. The label is kept. At inference, the prediction is the mean over K extra remasks of the test row (observed entries only). The averaging is meant to suppress shortcuts that depend on the exact pattern.

relations.counterfactual_prediction: Using uniform random masking that is not anchor-conditional should reduce the method to random augmentation. The held-out MNAR AP gap should then shrink to within 1 SE.
Using K=1 at inference should increase the Brier score and AP variance under reversed MNAR.
Under MAR validation, the method should not beat native HGB. If it loses by more than 0.01 AP, that falsifies the claim that the method is costless.

assumptions: Anchors are always observed and their relation to y is invariant across mechanisms.
Held-out MNAR changes only the masks, not P(x,y).
The sign of the mask-label correlation can differ between source and target.
The method should fail if missingness is the true causal signal (structural, grouped). In that case suppressing the mask throws away label information.
strongest_prior_art: arxiv:2507.08280 MIRRAMS: Overlap: both aim for robustness to unseen missingness shifts via label-relevant information. Difference: MIRRAMS uses MI conditions in a neural model. Ours conditions remasking on anchors in trees.
atom_39f339d257798e63 RoVTL: Overlap: missingness used as augmentation. Difference: RoVTL masks unconditionally and does not use test-time mask averaging.
algorithm: 1. Split rows 60/20/20 with a fixed seed. Fit g = per-anchor-quantile observed missing rate using training data only.
2. For r in 1..R=3, create a copy of the training set with M' ~ Bernoulli(g(anchor)*u), where u ~ U(0.5,2).
3. Stack the original rows and the remasked copies, with no reweighting and no scaler, so there is no cancellation.
4. Fit HGB with native NaN on the stacked data. Use early stopping on the validation mixture (clean, MCAR20, MCAR40, MAR).
5. At inference, for each row, draw K=8 extra anchor-conditional remasks of observed entries.
6. Predict as the mean of the probabilities across the K remasks.
7. Score the held-out mechanisms once. Their labels are never used for tuning.
8. Report AP, Brier, and clean AP over 10 seeds.
proposal.baseline: (a) Native-NaN HGB. (b) HGB with uniform random-mask augmentation at a matched expected rate and matched copy count. (c) Strongest constituent, impute-then-regress (atom_8ddbda79240111e1): mean imputation plus mask indicators, followed by HGB.
ablations: Edge removal: uniform remask instead of anchor-conditional, with matched rate and R.
Training remask removed, with test-time averaging only.
Matched copy count without remasking, to control for data volume.
proposal.metric: Primary: mean AP across the 3 held-out mechanisms. Secondary: Brier score and clean AP. The interaction is measured as Δ = gain(full) − gain(train-only) − gain(test-only), with a paired bootstrap across seeds.
proposal.falsification: The hypothesis is rejected if any of the following holds: the full method fails to beat uniform augmentation on mean held-out AP by at least 0.01 with the 95% CI excluding 0; the interaction Δ is ≤ 0; or clean AP drops by more than 0.01. A loss on grouped structural missingness is expected, and is predicted in advance as a failure case.
proposal.feasibility: About 4×3000 training rows and 20 features for HGB, plus K=8 predictions. This should take under 1 minute per seed on a laptop CPU.
